premises: A thermal pre-oxidation treatment at 300 °C for 1 hour in air forms a homogeneous, adherent iron oxide layer on Q235 steel.
This oxide film acts as a physical barrier limiting transport of corrosive species (oxygen, moisture, ions) to the steel substrate.
The oxide film reduces active sites for localized corrosion (e.g., pitting at grain boundaries or defects).
The protective effect is effective in high-humidity conditions at room temperature (25 °C) and moderately elevated temperature (75 °C).
The pre-oxidized Q235 steel will show lower corrosion rates (weight loss, pitting, EIS) than untreated steel under these conditions.
